headline: Petition to remove devices from pre-K through second grade sent to subcommittee for further review.
summary: The petition asks that student internet-connected devices be removed from pre-K through second-grade classrooms, with hands-on, teacher-led learning prioritized. Students with an IEP or Section 504 plan would keep their supports, and technology enrichment classes would not be affected. Members also approved a lease for 1,000 staff MacBooks and 6,000 student Chromebooks, and a 3-year extension of the Apptegy website contract at $157,500.
decisions: Approved the consent agenda after roll call.
Referred the Sullivan Middle School bathroom petition to Operations and Governance, 9-0.
Approved the Doherty Biomedical Academy program update, 3-0 in subcommittee.
Approved grants and other finance items, 9-0, including $175,000 for North High.
Referred the pre-K through second grade device petition to TLSS, 9-0.
Approved legal work for an employee's US work visa, up to $8,000, 9-0.
Approved a 3-year extension of the Apptegy website hosting contract at $157,500, 9-0.
Approved a lease to replace 1,000 staff MacBooks and 6,000 student Chromebooks, 9-0.
Approved a three-year CDW Government renewal for Lightspeed internet filtering, 9-0.
discussion: Devices in pre-K through second grade: Public speakers asked the committee to remove student devices in these grades and said students spend about 40 minutes a day on them in second grade. Members said they want more information on how devices are used, and some said classroom observations show hands-on learning.

Sullivan Middle School bathrooms: Eighth grade students presented a petition about broken toilets, missing soap, and privacy. They said their survey of 202 students found 62% had missed class while waiting to use the bathroom.

Chromebook lease: The administration said warranties on 23,000 Chromebooks bought in 2022 are expiring. It said the lease is already in this year's budget and that without it, many devices would be out of warranty next year.

Students leaving the district: The administration presented a report on students who withdrew or did not return. It said kindergarten withdrawals rose in SY25 and SY26 without a clear reason, and that enrollment is down about 650 students from October 1 of last year.
